schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: STAGE 1 OF THE CHART CHAIN, and a machine of its own since 2026-08-13. It answers ONE narrow question — what is actually being asked, and where does it live? — and emits the smallest typed artifact that fully determines what the next stage needs. The floor does not scan the territory itself: it COMPOSES cairn/tools/orient's device_census, so the roster is the settled measurer's, never a parallel scan. Emits the orient packet (intent/domain/scope/refs/unknowns) and refuses any ref the floor cannot verify EXISTS. Three strata, cheapest first: FLOOR (deterministic, this module), TREE (this nexus's own corpus through cairn/tools/tree), CEILING (the skill's assembly). The exit artifact berths in instance-space and the deposit-back lands it as the tree's memory of this class of request. THE FLOOR AUTHORS, AND PROVENANCE IS MEASURED (ticket orient-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured). Three of the five fields are lookup rather than language, so the floor WRITES them and does not merely report facts under them: ``refs`` (the paths it verified plus the homes of the components and skills it matched), ``domain`` (those addresses with their rung, read off the complexity axis), ``unknowns`` (what it could not ground). It authors nothing it cannot ground — an ambiguous component name becomes an unknown, never a guessed ref, because ``component_dir`` refuses the homonym loudly and a pointer that resolves to two places is not a pointer. ``intent`` and ``scope`` are NOT candidates and are not a to-do: restating an ask in grounded terms and drawing an in/out line are the two things that need a reader.
why: Akien, verbatim 2026-08-13: "orient is a machine. the other pre-build steps are each their own machine." A machine is tools plus the glue that holds them together, and that is exactly the shape here: cairn/tools/chain's grammar plus this stage's own question. THE LIVED SYMPTOM the whole chain answers is a build that starts before anyone settled what was being built — the web-server carrier miss, bounds-checking that never ran to completion. A stage that is its own machine can be fired, proved, and replaced alone; one that is a function in a 1,300-line module cannot. WHY THE RECORD AND NOT A COMPLAINT LIST (Akien, 2026-08-13): "passing such a thing without inspecting it means passing a mystery if something downstream fails … if every machine and even some more complex tools have their own inspector and gate, then each has documented and controllable quality validation … we can backtrack and see exactly where something went awry even if it's not something we're specifically looking for yet." A complaint list is empty both when every check passed and when no check ran, so the stage downstream is handed a mystery in exactly the case he named. The entries that PASSED are the ones nobody was looking for. "We might have to add more or better inspection questions, but that's fine. we learn as we go" — so the question list grows, and every addition is one more entry a reader sees whether it passed or failed.

feedback.why: THE UPSTREAM ARTIFACT IS THE TICKET — Akien, 2026-08-14, correcting this route's first cast: "orient's upstream artifacts should be the ticket. the ticketing machine would be the owner of that. and would get the feedback." MEASURED AND HE IS RIGHT ON DISK: the whole chain is keyed by ticket id, not by a conversation — `skills.chart.live chain <ticket-id>` is how the standing chain is found, every chart door refuses a packet whose ref'd berth claims a DIFFERENT ticket, the claim rides every link and may never silently vanish, and since 2026-07-29 the emit chokepoint refuses a BUILDME crossing with no berthed validate packet claiming the ticket. Building from the conversation is a build error the door itself throws. So stage 1's input is not 'the ask' loosely — it is that artifact, and it has an owner. STAGE 1 IS THE ONLY LEG WITH NO UPSTREAM STAGE, which is what sends this route out of the chain rather than back one link: measured 2026-08-14, every other leg's inspector opens on a ref into the berth before it (constrain intent_ref, survey constrain_ref, decompose survey_ref, triage decompose_ref, hypothesize triage_ref, validate hypothesize_ref, verdict validate_ref) and orient's opens on none. Akien's rule, 2026-08-14: "the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels." REFINED BY HIM THE SAME DAY, and the refinement is what `to` MEANS: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step." So this field is not a hop count and never was — it names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case, not the definition, and a route that lands elsewhere is not a special case needing a count. Orient is the case that shows why that refinement matters: its target is not N steps back, it is simply not in the chain at all. AND IT IS THE CASE HIS OWN MEASUREMENT FOUND DOMINANT — of askscan's five gaps, three were ambiguities in the REQUEST and belonged above the whole chain. WHAT THIS ROUTE SERVES: every_ref_exists_on_disk failing means the ticket named something nobody could resolve; authored_fields_are_non_empty_strings failing means it carried too little to orient on. Both are facts about the ticket and both are actionable by the hand that casts one. THE ADDRESS IS THE STORE BECAUSE THE OWNER IS NOT BUILT YET, and that is stated rather than blurred: he names a TICKETING MACHINE as the owner that would receive this, and no such component exists — cairn/machines/ holds build_inspector, diagnostic_inspector, learning_block, ruling and skill_block, and nothing casts or gates a ticket. So the route names CairnCommons/tickets, the artifact store the unbuilt machine would own, exactly as build_inspector's and ruling's do. When the ticketing machine is built, these three routes move to it in one act; until then this is the honest address and not a placeholder for one. WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH: the /chart ceiling that filled the packet is a hand, and a hand is not an address (cairn/tools/feedback edge (e)). WHO LAUNCHES ORIENT, since the launcher is not the target and the two are easy to conflate: /chart fires it as stage 1 (skills/chart/SKILL.md imports floor_facts and write_packet from this module), and /sail fires its brick loop mid-build when a correction surfaces ("a correction surfaced mid-build rides orient's brick loop (deposit → counsel → propose), never a quiet local fix"). Neither is the feedback target: a skill is a hand reading markdown. Note also the homonym — /sail's `cairn.tools.orient.orient git` is the census tool, a different component entirely.

invoke: fired by the skill that runs the chain; the writer door is write_packet; the inspector is inspect_orient(packet) and returns the proof record without taking a verdict, so a caller can READ what this stage proved without provoking its refusal
entry: Carved out of the chart machine on 2026-08-13 under Akien's ruling — "chart is a skill, it calls a collection of machines. that's the intention." The chart charter it was carved from is the design record of the whole chain and now berths with the skill at cairn/skills/chart/intention+why.json; this file holds only what is THIS component's.
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter, BORN AT THIS ADDRESS'S FIRST CROSSING. Until a ticket crosses here there is no journal, and that absence is this machine's ordinary resting state rather than a missing file — a component that has never sailed has no voyage to record. CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (ticket a-charter-may-not-assert-a-file-that-is-not-there): this sentence read 'Both were born at the carve-out', which was false — no journal has ever been born at a carve-out anywhere in the system. orient's arrived weeks after its carve-out, at its first crossing, and that is the mechanism for all eight. The fix is the sentence and never the files: an empty state.json here would manufacture a record of a voyage that did not happen (Law 7). The voyages that BUILT this stage before the carve-out are in the chart machine's history, which stays whole with the skill — a record of truth is never split.
gates: THE STAGE'S OWN INSPECTOR AND ITS OWN GATE, at this address (ruling 2026-08-13 every-machine-carries-its-own-inspector-and-gate). ``inspect_orient`` returns a PROOF RECORD — one entry per check that ran, EXPECTED beside ACTUAL, passes included — and ``validate_orient`` is the == compare over it, per entry, with no oracle anywhere near it. The shared half of the record comes from cairn/tools/chain's ``common_shape_record`` so the eight doors cannot drift apart; the stage-specific half is written here. Refusals still name every shape lack at once (ticket chart-doors-refuse-in-one-pass), and they are DERIVED from the record's mismatches, so the gate and the sentence it prints cannot disagree about what failed. A CHECK THAT DID NOT RUN IS ABSENT, NOT PASSED: guarded checks make the record SHORTER, never cleaner. AND THE ONE LABEL THE SENDER MAY NOT WRITE (ticket orient-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured). Provenance for ``refs``, ``domain`` and ``unknowns`` is DERIVED at this gate by re-running the floor over the packet's own ``request`` and comparing; a field claims ``floor`` only when the floor's answer can be REPRODUCED, and a sender that declares one and gets it wrong is refused rather than corrected — a silent overwrite would leave a sender still believing it labels its own work. It lives in ``validate_orient`` and not in ``write_packet`` because that is what makes it unavoidable: both doors a packet can leave by, the berth and the deposit-back, run this function. Refusal is on DISAGREEMENT, not on presence: a label matching the measurement is not a claim the sender made, and refusing it would make this door's own output illegal at the next door one line later. A ``tree`` declaration stands untouched — this measures floor-vs-claude and nothing else.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) this stage reading its input from anywhere but the previous stage's BERTHED packet; (2) a door that dribbles refusals instead of naming every lack in one pass; (3) a packet admitted whose provenance does not cover every authored field; (4) this module importing a sibling stage — the legs speak the grammar, never each other. (5) a check in this stage's inspector that PASSES SILENTLY — every check that ran appears in the record with its EXPECTED beside its ACTUAL, and a check that could not run is ABSENT rather than passed, so a check that stops running makes the record SHORTER and never cleaner; (6) a refusal sentence assembled from anywhere but the record's own mismatches — the gate and the sentence it prints cannot be allowed to disagree about what failed; (7) an oracle consulted anywhere on this path, at fire time or at sleep — `bin/cmd/determinism` must keep reading this component PURE DETERMINISTIC and REFUSES GATE. (8) any route by which a packet reaches a berth or the tree carrying a provenance label its sender wrote for refs/domain/unknowns — the self-report this build removed, restored; (9) the floor authoring a ref that does not exist, which is the worst failure available here because a fabrication would be wearing a MEASUREMENT's provenance; (10) the floor's grounded unknowns crowding out the ceiling's conceptual ones, so a packet reads as thoroughly ungrounded when what it actually lacks is a reader's judgement; (11) the derived floor fraction sitting at 0.00 across a corpus of post-door packets — the label became honest and the answer is still not reused, which is the whole point (watched by probes/floor_earns_its_label.py).
horizon: re-read when the chain's stage list changes, or when this stage's tree stratum goes live against a real embed seam.
how_it_learns: the deposit-back: every ceiling assembly deposits its own answer into this nexus's tree, so the next similar request walks to a settled answer instead of re-deriving it (Law 1 as runtime). The dial (cairn/skills/chart/dial.py) is the instrument that says whether the floor+tree fraction is actually growing — a nexus that never compiles is a ceiling doing the floor's job forever. AND THE DIAL NOW READS SOMETHING. Until 2026-08-14 that instrument was measuring a self-report: over 45 berthed packets, 44 declared ``refs: floor`` and 18 declared ``domain: floor``, 14 of the floor-labelled values ran past 200 characters of prose, and re-running the floor reproduced NOT ONE of them — the dial read 0.40 and the real code-produced fraction was 0.00. The number the staircase is steered by was computed by the party being measured (Law 3: an unmeasured claim is a hypothesis). Since the door derives it, a rising floor fraction is evidence about the floor and not about the ceiling's opinion of itself, and the second-order learning is the incentive that creates: the ONLY way for the ceiling to earn ``floor`` is to carry the floor's answer through unchanged, so the skill's prose and the door's measurement now pull the same direction. Not a token-cost argument — Claude is cached (ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap); the floor authoring makes the answer REUSABLE, which is what the tree deposits are made of and what the Hex ceiling will need to have already been true.

owner: CC owns this module's code and proofs and gates writes to them. Akien owns the ruling that made it a machine (decision 2026-08-13-chart-is-a-skill-that-calls-machines) and the chain's stage vocabulary.
proof: proofs/test_chart_orient.py, sealed by the tester in a netns; validation persisted in validations/. Nineteen teeth since 2026-08-14 (was fourteen): a declared ``floor`` label is refused and the same packet without it sails carrying the measured one; a field earns ``floor`` by reproducing and loses it to one added ref while surviving a reorder; a packet with no ``request`` can earn nothing; the floor never authors a ref that does not exist; an ambiguous name becomes exactly one unknown and no ref. The fixture also moved onto real rungs in the same act — it had been building ``cairn/<name>/``, a shape the house stopped having on 2026-08-13, which nothing had noticed because nothing yet read the rung.
